How long does a widget last?

The lifespan of a widget depends on far more than the material it is made from, and before we get to numbers it is worth explaining how we tested, because the method shapes every result that follows. We bought twelve widgets from six brands, mounted each on an identical bench, and ran them through a daily routine of clamping, cutting and sanding for six months. Every week we measured play in the jaws, wear on the thread, noise under load and heat after an hour of work, and we logged every failure along with the conditions that caused it. Some widgets failed early because of poor casting, others because of weak springs, and a few lasted the whole test without any measurable wear at all. The steel models held up best overall, though two aluminium models came close, and the plastic models wore fastest under heavy use but were perfectly adequate for light hobby work on weekends.
